idiom_name: package-level registry map populated from init() (the database/sql driver shape)
implementation_notes: Go has no container, but it has a house idiom for the classic structure: a package-private map guarded by a mutex (or sync.Map) plus exported Register and lookup functions, with implementations registering themselves from init() and the caller selecting one by name - exactly what database/sql does with sql.Register(name, driver), the blank import that triggers it, and sql.Open(driverName, dsn) resolving through the drivers map. Reach for that shape for drivers, codecs and plugins selected by configuration or a blank import; inside application code, pass collaborators as struct fields or constructor parameters, which is what the standard library does everywhere except its registries. A hand-rolled generic container is not idiomatic Go: no reflection-based wiring and no type-keyed maps are needed when the graph is built once in main.
pitfalls: Self-registration happens in init(), so the available services depend on blank imports; a forgotten import surfaces at run time as an unknown-key error (database/sql even words it "forgotten import?").
Duplicate names overwrite silently unless checked - the standard library panics on a duplicate driver name precisely because last-registration-wins hides misconfiguration.
The map is shared mutable state: finish registration before serving goroutines and guard reads, or a race appears under load that never shows in single-threaded tests.
